description:
The annual Brahmotsavams are celebrated for 11 days, typically in February or March. The 2026 schedule spanned from 18 February to 28 February 2026:
Day 1 (18 Feb): Swasti Vachanam, Vishwaksena Aradhana, Ankurarpanam, Raksha Bandhanam (seed sowing and sacred thread tying).
Day 2 (19 Feb): Dhwajarohanam (hoisting of the Garuda flag on the temple mast) & Bheri Puja.
Day 3 (20 Feb): Matsyavataram Alankaram & Sri Sesha Vahana Seva (deity adorned in fish incarnation on serpent vehicle).
Day 4 (21 Feb): Vatapatrashayi Alankaram & Sri Hamsa Vahana Seva (deity adorned as baby Krishna on banyan leaf on swan vehicle).
Day 5 (22 Feb): Sri Krishna Alankaram & Sri Simha Vahana Seva (deity adorned as Lord Krishna on lion vehicle).
Day 6 (23 Feb): Govardhanagiridhari Alankaram & Sri Gaja Vahana Seva (deity adorned as Govardhan hill lifter on elephant vehicle).
Day 7 (24 Feb): Edurukolu Mahotsavam (traditional welcoming ceremony between the families of the bride and bridegroom).
Day 8 (25 Feb): Thiru Kalyanotsavam (the grand celestial wedding of Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy).
Day 9 (26 Feb): Divya Vimana Rathotsavam (the grand chariot festival around the hillock).
Day 10 (27 Feb): Maha Purnahuti, followed by Chakra Teertham (holy immersion of the Sudarshana Chakra in the temple tank).
Day 11 (28 Feb): Shataghata Abhishekam, followed by Dolotsavam (Swing festival) & Official Conclusion.
importance: The most prominent and prestigious annual festival of the temple, commemorating the divine manifestation and celestial wedding (Thiru Kalyanotsavam) of Lord Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy, attracting lakhs of pilgrims across the country.

description: Celebrated on Vaishakha Shukla Chaturdashi (occurring on Tuesday, 18 May 2027). The festival honors the manifestation of the Lord at dusk. Special Nijabhisekam, Laksha Tulasi Archana, and Vadapappu-Panakam distribution take place.
importance: Celebrates the divine incarnation of Lord Narasimha appearing at twilight to protect Prahlada and destroy evil; considered the most sacred day for overcoming obstacles, fear, and negative energies.

description: Performed monthly on the birth star of the Lord (Swathi). A grand Kalyanotsavam is performed on this day, attracting massive crowds of local devotees.
importance: Honors the Janma Nakshatram (birth star) of Lord Narasimha with sacred Shataghatabhishekam and celestial wedding rituals, believed to bestow family harmony, prosperity, and spiritual well-being.

description: Massive congregations gather for the Uttara Dwara Darshanam (Vaikuntha Ekadashi).
importance: One of the most revered Vaishnavite festivals; walking through the Uttara Dwaram (Northern Gate) on this auspicious day is believed to grant direct darshan of Lord Vishnu and pave the path to Moksha (liberation).
